## This week

Orientation (grading, weekly rhythm, presentation assignment) followed by the first lecture: what separates an agent from a chatbot. An agent is a system whose control flow is decided by the model's output; the lecture builds that definition from what an LLM call can and cannot do, then covers the agent loop, the components (Model · Instructions · Tools · Memory), the autonomy spectrum, workflow patterns, and form factors — and closes with the course map: build the agent (W2–4), discipline it (W5), scale it (W6–7), ground and operate it (W9–13).

The lecture notes are available online and as Markdown or PDF. The slides open in Google Slides.

## Lab

`W1_lab_setup.ipynb` — first calls through `aisuite`; message roles, statelessness, temperature; and a final task: a system prompt that makes every answer come back as clean JSON, checked PASS/FAIL.

Click *Open in Colab* in the table above — the notebook opens directly in Colab. Save your own copy first (**File → Save a copy in Drive**) so your work persists; the `.ipynb` download stays available for local Jupyter. Then paste your API key into the setup cell and run the notebook top to bottom. **Prerequisite:** your own API key — follow the [API Setup Guide](api-setup.qmd) *before* class.

## Presentations

No paper presentation in Week 1. Presenter slots are assigned during orientation, and presentations begin in Week 2 with Chain-of-Thought ([Wei et al., 2022](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.11903) ([PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2201.11903))) and Self-Consistency ([Wang et al., 2022](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.11171) ([PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2203.11171))).
